definitions.gloss: disgraceful behavior; shameful sight; ugly spectacle
definitions.explanation: An embarrassing or shameful display of conduct, especially one witnessed by others. Often used when someone loses composure or behaves in a way that brings shame.

examples.english: To make a spectacle of oneself.

examples.japanese: {酔|よ}って{醜態|しゅうたい}を{演|えん}じてしまった。
examples.english: I got drunk and made a disgraceful scene.

examples.japanese: {大勢|おおぜい}の{前|まえ}で{醜態|しゅうたい}をさらすのは{二度|にど}とごめんだ。
examples.english: I never want to embarrass myself in front of a crowd again.

notes:
Describes a shameful or unsightly display of behavior, particularly when witnessed by others. Composed of {醜|しゅう} (ugly) + {態|たい} (appearance/state). Carries a strong negative connotation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {醜態|しゅうたい}をさらす: to expose one's disgraceful behavior; to make a spectacle of oneself
- {醜態|しゅうたい}を{演|えん}じる: to put on a disgraceful display
- {醜態|しゅうたい}をさらけ{出|だ}す: to lay bare one's shameful behavior

USAGE:
Most commonly appears in the fixed expression {醜態|しゅうたい}をさらす. Often used in contexts involving drunkenness, public failures, or loss of composure. The word has a literary or formal tone and is more common in written language and news reporting than casual speech.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {失態|しったい}: blunder, gaffe — focuses on a mistake rather than the visual ugliness of the behavior
- {恥|はじ}: shame, disgrace — more general and common in everyday speech
